usage: SECOND OFFLINE WORKSHOP ONLY. Untested editorial candidates, not medical authority or validated learning aids. No automatic production injection. Held/rejected terms are not usable cue recommendations. Raw proposal pronunciation text predates main-agent source checks; see guide.
excluded_terms: clock tower as generic neurological cue

sources.scope: Target pronunciation and word parts only, not endorsement of cue or medical lesson grounding.
Headword and shared object/anatomy senses only.
Headword and shared appliance/element senses only.
Medical use of the balloon headword only; no procedural facts or treatment instructions imported.

entries.decision_reason: Vane/vein is a plausible complete homophone without missing stress, but the specified rooftop object may be named weathercock, arrow, wind indicator, or weather vane rather than vane. This is the same exact-noun dependency that held socket/outlet and rod/pole previously. No label-free naming evidence resolves it. No exact stale target or object duplicate found; a possible bird-shaped vane must not inherit an existing bird cue. Only vein identity is proposed, not any vessel property or subtype.

attempts.pronunciation_caveat: Provisional, not source-checked: vane and vein are expected whole-word homophones in ordinary English.
attempts.recognition_risk: A viewer may say weathercock, arrow, or wind indicator instead of vane; no label may supply the missing name.
attempts.reason: Whole-word homophone, not a constructed rebus. One familiar drawable object can supply the complete sound without edits, conditional on unprompted vane naming. Encodes only the anatomical headword, not vessel subtype or function.

Assuming an unseen draining action would violate the criterion. Mesh/grate appearance may overlap the prior nitrate grate or catalog filtration/retention cues; this is a predicted collision, not an observed failure. Retain the previous strict naming standard rather than accepting a caption. No particular device or procedure is recoverable.

entries.decision_reason: The whole plural sound can match, but bee boxes, nests, and beehives are plausible unprompted names. Plural naming must arise naturally; a two-object count is not proof of plural-word recovery, consistent with the previous pons/pawns hold. Hive imagery can evoke the bees already used for rabies and rejected scabies; no transmission or cause follows. No exact stale target or hive-object mapping found. Hold for noun/plural recovery and cross-cue discrimination, not merely because the target is generic.

entries.decision_reason: The saved tape roll plus worm plausibly supplies both complete ordinary object names in order without deleting consonants, changing major vowels, or losing stressed material. Sticky/adhesive tape retains tape; roll or caterpillar responses remain untested risks. No exact prior target/object duplicate found. The shared worm component must be discriminated against hookworm and whipworm using the first object, not a suffix-only response. This is spelling/word-part assembly, not evidence of cause, transmission, morphology, taxonomy, novelty, or recall benefit.

attempts.pronunciation_caveat: PROVISIONAL: tentative TAYP-wurm preserves both complete object names in order; compound stress and the speaker's worm vowel need verification. Not dictionary-checked.
attempts.recognition_risk: The roll may be named adhesive, roll, or sticky tape; the worm may be named caterpillar or snake. A visibly separate pair still needs uncoached left-to-right recovery testing.
attempts.reason: CONSTRUCTED COMPOUND REBUS, not a homophone or homonym. Both full word parts have familiar drawable referents, with no omitted consonant or syllable under the provisional reading. Identity only: tape is not a proposed cause, source, transmission vehicle, or biological description. Distinct headword, not a plural or synonym variant. Independent screening remains required.

entries.decision_reason: Hook plus worm covers the full compound without a necessary sound repair, but the familiar hook/worm pairing can instead elicit bait or fishing, and the worm can be named bait rather than worm. The exact component sequence is therefore not established by familiarity alone. Fishing imagery also overlaps the previous rod cue, while worm is shared with the other two current compounds. No exact stale target mapping found. Hold for uncoached object naming, complete-compound recovery and distractor discrimination; do not infer any biological claim.

attempts.reason: CONSTRUCTED COMPOUND REBUS, not a homophone or homonym. Two familiar objects supply the complete provisional sound sequence. Identity only: neither a fishing association nor a hook asserts cause, transmission, anatomy, or taxonomy. The fishing/bait intrusion is unresolved, not evidence of a pass. Distinct headword rather than a synonym variant; independent screening remains required.

entries.decision_reason: Whip plus worm can preserve the full sound sequence; WH/W variation alone is not a defect when both component and target are spoken consistently by the learner. The blocking issue is whip versus rope/cord/lash naming and worm versus caterpillar/snake, not a missing stressed syllable. Rope appearance also risks overlap with the previous sinus noose or sertraline rope proposals; all current worm compounds need first-object discrimination. No exact stale target mapping found. No corrective prop, inferred whipping action, or biological interpretation is added.

attempts.pronunciation_caveat: PROVISIONAL: tentative WHIP-wurm preserves both full object names; speakers may distinguish WH from W, and compound stress needs verification. Not dictionary-checked.

attempts.reason: CONSTRUCTED COMPOUND REBUS, not a homophone or homonym. Both complete word parts are drawable without labels, named faces, or an inferred action. Identity only: whip supplies a noun sound, not an act, cause, biological shape claim, or taxonomic claim. Distinct headword rather than a synonym variant; independent screening remains required.
